TOS4_Section2.text: What analytical technique is used on a balance to accurately measure the mass of a hydroscopic or volatile sample by weighing a container before and after transferring its contents?
options: A. Direct weighing
B. Weighing by difference
C. Taring the balance with the sample inside
D. Buoyancy correction weighing

TOS4_Section2.text: Why must a hot sample (e.g., freshly removed from a drying oven) NEVER be weighed directly on an analytical balance?
options: A. The heat will melt the weighing pan.
B. Convection currents create upward air forces against the balance pan, causing the apparent mass to read falsely low.
C. The balance computer will register an electrical short circuit.
D. Hot objects absorb weight from the atmosphere.

TOS4_Section2.text: Before using a clean glass volumetric pipette to transfer a standard solution, why should the pipette be rinsed with a small portion of the solution itself (conditioning)?
options: A. To cool the glass down to room temperature
B. To coat the internal surface and remove any residual distilled water droplets that would dilute the transferred solution
C. To increase the viscosity of the liquid
D. To etch the calibration line more clearly

TOS4_Section2.text: What is the proper technique for pouring a liquid from a reagent bottle into a narrow-mouthed container to prevent liquid from running down the outside of the bottle?
options: A. Tilt the bottle quickly and pour from the side facing the paper label.
B. Hold a glass stirring rod against the lip of the bottle and pour the liquid down the rod.
C. Use a plastic syringe to suck liquid out of the rim.
D. Warm the bottle neck with a heat gun before pouring.

TOS4_Section2.text: Why is it strictly forbidden to return unused excess chemical reagent from your bench back into the original manufacturer's stock bottle?
options: A. The reagent loses its molar mass over time.
B. It risks contaminating the entire stock supply with impurities or moisture collected at the work station.
C. Stock bottles are legally sealed after opening.
D. Unused reagents undergo spontaneous radioactive decay.

TOS4_Section2.text: What safety hazard is introduced when closing the glass doors of an analytical balance while weighing a hygroscopic powder?
options: A. Closing the doors eliminates draft disturbances, ensuring stable, accurate readings.
B. Enclosing hygroscopic powders causes them to explode.
C. Draft shielding prevents the analytical balance from measuring atmospheric pressure.
D. Closed doors trap moisture against the sample.

TOS4_Section2.text: Which piece of glassware is calibrated to CONTAIN a specified exact volume at a stated temperature, rather than to DELIVER that volume?
options: A. Burette
B. Volumetric pipette
C. Volumetric flask
D. Mohr pipette

TOS4_Section2.text: When pipetting any liquid in a chemistry laboratory, what suction device should always be used?
options: A. Direct mouth suction
B. Rubber bulb or mechanical pipette filler
C. Lung inhalation through a flexible tube
D. Exhalation pressure from a syringe

TOS4_Section2.text: What is the primary purpose of performing a 'quantitative transfer' during gravimetric or volumetric sample preparation?
options: A. To speed up the evaporation of solvent
B. To ensure 100% of the solid or liquid sample is transferred without loss by rinsing the weighing vessel and funnel multiple times
C. To neutralize any acid present in the solution
D. To mix two immiscible layers together

TOS4_Section2.text: How should the glass stopper of a liquid reagent bottle be handled when pouring a chemical to avoid contamination of the benchtop?
options: A. Placed flat on its side directly on the wooden workbench surface.
B. Held between the fingers or placed upside down on a clean watch glass.
C. Dropped into a sink filled with water.
D. Clamped tightly to a ring stand.

TOS4_Section2.text: Which glassware is classified as suitable ONLY for approximate volume estimation and should never be used for quantitative analytical measurements?
options: A. Analytical burette
B. Griffin low-form glass beaker
C. Volumetric pipette
D. Class A volumetric flask

TOS4_Section2.text: What essential information must be included on the label of a temporary chemical working solution prepared in a laboratory beaker?
options: A. Chemical name or formula, concentration, date prepared, and preparer's initials/hazard warnings
B. Market price of the chemical and supplier name
C. Molecular weight and melting point only
D. Room number and instructor's home address

TOS4_Section2.text: If a student reads the meniscus from an elevated standing position instead of looking straight across at eye level, what measurement error occurs?
options: A. Parallax error, resulting in a reading that is falsely low
B. Parallax error, resulting in a reading that is falsely high
C. Calibration drift error
D. Temperature-induced volume expansion

TOS4_Section2.text: What is the correct method for transferring a dry solid powder into a volumetric flask with a narrow neck?
options: A. Pour the solid directly from the beaker without a funnel.
B. Use a clean glass powder funnel and rinse any residual solid through with solvent into the flask.
C. Dissolve the solid in water inside a closed bottle first, then freeze it.
D. Blow the powder through a glass tube into the flask.

TOS4_Section2.text: How does density factor into liquid measurements when converting between mass and volume?
options: A. Mass equals volume divided by density.
B. Mass equals density multiplied by volume (m = d × V).
C. Density equals mass multiplied by volume squared.
D. Volume equals mass multiplied by density squared.

TOS4_Section2.text: Why should a chemical balance never be adjusted or overloaded beyond its maximum specified capacity?
options: A. It permanently damages the internal knife-edges, strain gauges, and electronic weighing mechanism.
B. It causes the balance to emit a bright ultraviolet light.
C. It converts the weighed sample into gas.
D. It reverses the polarity of the digital display screen.

TOS4_Section2.text: When handling corrosive liquids or concentrated acids, what personal protective equipment (PPE) is mandatory in addition to standard safety goggles and a lab coat?
options: A. Open-toed sandals and shorts
B. Chemical-resistant gloves and a face shield
C. Heavy wool winter jacket
D. Earplugs and a dust mask

TOS4_Section2.text: What is the primary difference between a blue flame and a yellow flame on a Bunsen burner?
options: A. The yellow flame is hotter and indicates complete combustion.
B. The blue flame is hotter, cleaner, and indicates complete combustion with adequate air intake.
C. The yellow flame uses pure oxygen instead of air.
D. The blue flame is only used for melting glass tubing.

TOS4_Section2.text: Which heating method is safest and most appropriate for boiling a low-boiling, highly flammable organic solvent like diethyl ether (bp 35 °C)?
options: A. Direct Bunsen burner flame
B. Electric hot plate or water/steam bath
C. High-temperature metal block
D. Microwave irradiation

TOS4_Section2.text: What variable electrical device is typically used to control the power output and heating rate of a round-bottom flask heating mantle?
options: A. Variable transformer (Variac)
B. pH meter controller
C. Magnetic stirrer rheostat
D. Step-down transformer for DC power

TOS4_Section2.text: What severe hazard occurs if a small amount of water accidentally splashes into a hot silicone oil bath operating at 180 °C?
options: A. The water instantly freezes the oil into a solid block.
B. The water rapidly vaporizes, causing dangerous hot oil splattering.
C. The oil undergoes spontaneous catalytic combustion.
D. The oil bath temperature drops instantly to 0 °C.

TOS4_Section2.text: What is the approximate temperature range achieved by a cooling bath composed of crushed ice and common salt (NaCl)?
options: A. 0 °C to -5 °C

TOS4_Section2.text: What approximate temperature is maintained using a cooling bath consisting of dry ice (solid carbon dioxide) mixed with acetone or isopropanol?
What primary cryogenic and safety hazard is associated with working with liquid nitrogen in a poorly ventilated small laboratory room?
options: A. Production of poisonous chlorine gas
B. Rapid asphyxiation due to oxygen displacement and condensation of liquid oxygen
C. Immediate ignition of all plastic tubing
D. Spontaneous polymerization of surrounding air

TOS4_Section2.text: Why is it dangerous to immediately plunge a glowing-hot borosilicate glass round-bottom flask directly into an ice-water bath?
options: A. The ice melts instantly.
B. Thermal shock causes uneven glass contraction, resulting in cracking or shattering.
C. The solvent inside freezes and expands to break the neck.
D. It generates high-voltage static electricity.

TOS4_Section2.text: Why is an ice-water slurry a much more effective cooling medium for a round-bottom flask than dry chunks of ice alone?
options: A. Ice-water provides maximum physical surface contact area around the curved glass walls of the flask.
B. Pure ice has a temperature of +10 °C.
C. Water acts as a chemical catalyst to freeze the flask faster.
D. Dry ice floats away from the glass surface.

TOS4_Section2.text: What dangerous physical property of hot laboratory glassware frequently leads to accidental skin burns?
options: A. Hot glass glows bright red, warning users of high temperatures.
B. Hot glass looks identical in appearance to cold glass.
C. Hot glass emits a loud buzzing sound when touched.
D. Hot glass feels icy cold due to rapid thermal conduction.

TOS4_Section2.text: What catastrophic accident happens if any chemical apparatus is heated while completely sealed off from the atmosphere?
options: A. The internal vacuum causes the glassware to implode.
B. Thermal expansion of gases and vapors generates high pressure, causing a violent explosion.
C. The solvent condenses into a solid crystal lattice.
D. The heating source automatically shuts off.

TOS4_Section2.text: Which heating setup is best suited for maintaining uniform heating of a round-bottom flask at temperatures between 150 °C and 250 °C without open flames?
options: A. Open Bunsen burner flame
B. Water bath
C. Silicone oil bath or heating mantle
D. Direct sunlight with a magnifying glass

TOS4_Section2.text: What is the primary purpose of adding boiling chips or a magnetic stir bar to a liquid before heating?
options: A. To raise the freezing point of the liquid
B. To promote smooth boiling and prevent superheating and violent bumping
C. To neutralize acidic impurities
D. To act as a temperature indicator dye

TOS4_Section2.text: Why should volumetric glassware (such as volumetric flasks or burettes) NEVER be heated on a hot plate or in an oven?
options: A. Heat causes the glass to dissolve in water.
B. Thermal expansion permanently alters the calibrated volume tolerances.
C. Volumetric glass turns opaque upon gentle warming.
D. It releases toxic lead fumes.

TOS4_Section2.text: When heating a liquid inside a small test tube using a Bunsen burner, how should the test tube be oriented?
options: A. Pointed straight upward toward your face to monitor bubbling closely
B. Pointed horizontally or away from yourself and others at an angle, with constant agitation
C. Placed flat on the lab bench while the flame touches the bottom
D. Sealed tightly with a rubber stopper

TOS4_Section2.text: What is the correct protocol when setting up equipment to manage a highly exothermic chemical reaction?
options: A. Add all reagents rapidly at once and remove cooling baths.
B. Keep a suitable cooling bath prepared nearby, add reagents slowly with stirring, and monitor temperature.
C. Heat the reaction vigorously to drive the exotherm to completion.
D. Seal the reaction vessel tightly to trap evolved heat.

TOS4_Section2.text: Why is a steam bath or water bath preferred over an electric hot plate when working with low-boiling flammable solvents?
options: A. Steam baths are completely incapable of transferring heat to organic liquids.
B. They provide a gentle, strictly controlled temperature ceiling (≤ 100 °C) with zero open flame or hot electric element ignition risks.
C. Water baths increase the reaction rate by 1000-fold.
D. They eliminate the need for boiling chips.

TOS4_Section2.text: What strict safety rule applies when storing or handling solid dry ice (solid CO₂) in the laboratory?
options: A. Always store dry ice in a tightly sealed glass container to prevent sublimation loss.
B. Never seal dry ice in an airtight container because sublimation generates extreme gas pressure leading to explosion.
C. Always handle dry ice with bare hands to test its temperature.
D. Dissolve dry ice in concentrated nitric acid before disposal.

TOS4_Section2.text: Why is a laboratory glass thermometer strictly forbidden from being used as a stirring rod?
options: A. Stirring with a thermometer causes it to record false high temperatures.
B. The thin glass bulb is easily broken, risking lacerations and hazardous mercury or spirit spills.
C. Glass thermometers absorb organic solutes from solution.
D. Friction bends the metal scale inside.

TOS4_Section2.text: What residual risk remains when using an electric hot plate to heat flammable organic solvents, even though it lacks an open flame?
options: A. Hot plate surfaces can degrade and emit radioactive alpha particles.
B. The surface temperature of the hot plate can easily exceed the autoignition temperature of volatile solvent vapors.
C. Electric hot plates generate magnetic fields that decompose organic bonds.
D. Hot plates freeze surrounding air moisture.

TOS5_Section1.text: In normal-phase adsorption thin-layer chromatography (TLC) using a polar stationary phase like silica gel, how do polar and nonpolar compounds behave?
options: A. Polar compounds move faster, while nonpolar compounds stick tightly to the plate.
B. Polar compounds interact more strongly with the stationary phase and move slower, while nonpolar compounds move faster.
C. Polar and nonpolar compounds travel at identical rates regardless of the eluent.
D. Nonpolar compounds dissolve completely in the silica gel matrix.

TOS5_Section1.text: What distinguishes reversed-phase chromatography from normal-phase chromatography?
options: A. Reversed-phase uses a nonpolar stationary phase (such as C18) with a polar mobile phase, causing polar compounds to elute first.
B. Reversed-phase uses water as the stationary phase and air as the mobile phase.
C. Reversed-phase allows compounds to travel backward down the plate.
D. Reversed-phase eliminates the need for any solvent system.

TOS5_Section1.text: Arrange the following common chromatography solvents in order of INCREASING eluent strength (polarity):
options: A. Water < Methanol < Ethyl acetate < Hexane
B. Hexane < Dichloromethane < Ethyl acetate < Water
C. Acetone < Toluene < Hexane < Methanol
D. Diethyl ether < Hexane < Acetone < Toluene

TOS5_Section1.text: Which class of organic compounds generally exhibits the highest polarity and slowest migration on a normal-phase silica TLC plate?
options: A. Saturated alkanes
B. Alkyl halides
C. Carboxylic acids
D. Ethers

TOS5_Section1.text: Why must a TLC plate baseline always be drawn using a pencil rather than a standard ink pen?
options: A. Pencil lead catalyzes chemical reactions on the plate.
B. Ink components are organic dyes that would dissolve in the developing solvent and run up the plate along with the sample.
C. Pencil marks are fluorescent under UV light.
D. Ink destroys the silica gel coating.

TOS5_Section1.text: Why must the initial liquid solvent level in a developing TLC chamber be maintained strictly BELOW the pencil baseline where spots are applied?
options: A. To prevent the spots from dissolving directly into the solvent pool rather than traveling by capillary action.
B. To speed up the evaporation rate of the solvent front.
C. To prevent the glass chamber from cracking.
D. To keep the solvent front from reaching the top too quickly.

TOS5_Section1.text: Calculate the Retention Factor ($R_f$) for a compound whose spot traveled 4.5 cm from the baseline, while the solvent front migrated 7.5 cm.
What is considered the ideal $R_f$ range for a target compound when optimizing solvent polarity for a column chromatography separation?
options: D. Exactly 0.95

TOS5_Section1.text: Which chemical visualization reagent is specifically used on TLC plates to detect amino acids and amines, yielding purple or brown spots?
options: A. Iodine vapor
B. Ninhydrin
C. Potassium permanganate (KMnO₄)
D. Anisaldehyde

TOS5_Section1.text: What is the primary cause of 'streaking' or 'tailing' of spots on a TLC plate?
options: A. Using too little sample or an excessively nonpolar solvent.
B. Overloading the sample spot, presence of acidic/basic compounds, or using a spotting solvent that is too polar.
C. Placing the chamber in a dark room.
D. Leaving the plate in the chamber after the solvent front reaches the top.

TOS5_Section1.text: What is the purpose of 'co-spotting' an unknown sample alongside an authentic reference standard on a TLC plate?
options: A. To determine the exact boiling point of the mixture.
B. To confirm identity; if both travel as a single, uniform spot in multiple solvent systems, they are likely the same compound.
C. To neutralize acidic impurities in the sample.
D. To double the migration speed of the solvent front.

TOS5_Section1.text: In column chromatography using silica gel, which type of compound elutes from the column first?
options: A. The most polar compound
B. The least polar (nonpolar) compound
C. The compound with the highest molecular weight
D. Compounds elute randomly regardless of polarity.

TOS5_Section1.text: Why is the wet (slurry) packing method generally preferred over dry packing when preparing a silica gel chromatography column?
options: A. Wet packing completely eliminates air bubbles and micro-channels that ruin separation efficiency.
B. Wet packing requires zero solvent usage.
C. Wet packing allows the column to operate at zero pressure.
D. Wet packing prevents silica gel from dissolving.

TOS5_Section1.text: What catastrophic problem occurs if a chromatography column is allowed to 'run dry' (solvent level drops below the top of the silica bed)?
options: A. The purified compounds turn into solid crystals inside the glass.
B. Cracks and air channels form in the silica bed, destroying uniform flow and ruining the separation.
C. The stopcock melts permanently.
D. The eluent changes into pure water.

TOS5_Section1.text: How should a solid sample be loaded onto the top of a column chromatography bed for optimal band resolution?
options: A. Dumped in as a thick, dry solid pile at the top.
B. Dissolved in the minimum possible volume of starting solvent (or dry-loaded onto silica) to form a very narrow, concentrated band.
C. Diluted in 500 mL of solvent to flood the column.
D. Mixed directly with the bottom layer of glass wool.

TOS5_Section1.text: What is the key operational feature of 'flash chromatography' compared to standard gravity column chromatography?
options: A. It uses compressed air or nitrogen gas to force solvent through the column rapidly, improving speed and resolution.
B. It is performed at extremely high cryogenic temperatures.
C. It uses an open flame to boil the eluent.
D. It eliminates the stationary phase entirely.

TOS5_Section1.text: When purifying a basic amine compound that might bind too strongly to acidic silica gel, which stationary phase grade of alumina is most appropriate?
options: A. Acidic alumina
B. Basic alumina
C. Neutral alumina
D. Coarse glass beads

TOS5_Section1.text: Which design modification increases the resolving power (separation efficiency) of a column chromatography system?
options: A. Using a shorter, wider column with larger silica particles.
B. Using a longer, narrower column with smaller, uniform adsorbent particles.
C. Removing the bottom layer of sand.
D. Increasing the sample mass by 1000%.

TOS5_Section1.text: What primary health and safety hazard is associated with handling fine, dry silica gel powder during column preparation?
options: A. Flammability upon skin contact
B. Severe respiratory hazard (silicosis/lung irritation from fine dust inhalation)
C. Rapid absorption through intact skin leading to systemic toxicity
D. Strong radioactive alpha emission

TOS5_Section1.text: If an organic compound yields only a single spot on a TLC plate developed in three different solvent systems, what preliminary conclusion can be drawn?
options: A. The compound is 100% pure beyond any doubt.
B. The compound is likely pure or consists of components with identical $R_f$ values in those systems.
C. The compound has decomposed into inorganic salts.
D. The stationary phase is defective.

TOS5_Section2.text: What is the correct sequential order of component parts through which the carrier gas and sample flow in a gas chromatograph?
options: A. Column oven -> Injection port -> Detector -> Carrier gas supply
B. Carrier gas supply -> Injection port -> Column in temperature-controlled oven -> Detector -> Data system
C. Detector -> Column -> Injection port -> Gas supply -> Recorder
D. Injection port -> Detector -> Column -> Gas cylinder

TOS5_Section2.text: Which property is essential for a carrier gas used in gas-liquid chromatography (GLC)?
options: A. It must be a strongly reactive oxidizing agent.
B. It must be completely inert, pure, dry, and chemically compatible with the detector.
C. It must have a high boiling point above 250 °C.
D. It must be colored to track flow visually.

TOS5_Section2.text: How do open tubular (capillary) columns compare functionally to packed columns in gas chromatography?
options: A. Capillary columns have lower efficiency and much higher sample capacity.
B. Capillary columns provide significantly higher theoretical plate efficiency and resolution, but have lower sample capacity.
C. Capillary columns cannot be used with mass spectrometers.
D. Capillary columns require liquid mobile phases.

TOS5_Section2.text: On a standard nonpolar capillary column (e.g., polydimethylsiloxane), in what general order do organic compounds elute?
options: A. In order of increasing boiling point
B. In order of increasing water solubility
C. In order of decreasing molecular weight
D. Strictly by decreasing dipole moment

TOS5_Section2.text: Which GC detector is destructive, highly sensitive to organic compounds containing C-H bonds, but completely insensitive to water and permanent inorganic gases?
options: A. Thermal Conductivity Detector (TCD)
B. Electron Capture Detector (ECD)
C. Flame Ionization Detector (FID)
D. Nitrogen-Phosphorus Detector (NPD)

TOS5_Section2.text: What is a major advantage of the Thermal Conductivity Detector (TCD) over a Flame Ionization Detector (FID)?
options: A. TCD is 1,000 times more sensitive than FID.
B. TCD is universal (detects any substance with thermal conductivity different from carrier gas) and is non-destructive.
C. TCD does not require a carrier gas.
D. TCD operates at room temperature without electrical power.

TOS5_Section2.text: Which GC detector exhibits extreme sensitivity and selectivity toward halogenated organic compounds, such as chlorinated pesticides and solvents?
options: A. Flame Ionization Detector (FID)
B. Electron Capture Detector (ECD)
C. Thermal Conductivity Detector (TCD)
D. Flame Photometric Detector (FPD)

TOS5_Section2.text: What fundamental analytical information does the retention time ($t_r$) of a chromatographic peak provide in gas chromatography?
options: A. Quantitative concentration based on peak height
B. Qualitative identification by comparison with known standards under identical conditions
C. Purity percentage of the carrier gas
D. Total molecular mass of the sample ion

TOS5_Section2.text: In quantitative gas chromatography, what physical attribute of a chromatographic peak is directly proportional to the amount (concentration) of the analyte?
options: A. Peak width at half-height only
B. Peak area or peak height
C. Total retention time
D. Dead time of the column

TOS5_Section2.text: What is the purpose of employing 'temperature programming' during a GC run of a sample containing compounds with a very wide boiling point range?
options: A. To keep the column temperature permanently frozen at -20 °C
B. To gradually increase the oven temperature over time, sharpening late-eluting peaks and reducing analysis time
C. To prevent the carrier gas from expanding
D. To melt the silica stationary phase

TOS5_Section2.text: Which primary requirement must an organic analyte satisfy to be successfully analyzed directly by standard gas chromatography?
options: A. It must be ionic and water-soluble.
B. It must be sufficiently volatile and thermally stable without decomposing at vaporization temperatures.
C. It must be a high-molecular-weight polymer.
D. It must absorb ultraviolet light strongly.

TOS5_Section2.text: Why is a 'split injection' technique commonly used when introducing liquid samples into a high-efficiency capillary GC column?
options: A. To divide the sample into two separate detectors simultaneously
B. To prevent column overload by venting a major fraction of the vaporized sample out the split vent, allowing only a small fraction onto the column
C. To split the carrier gas into hydrogen and oxygen
D. To freeze the sample before injection

TOS5_Section2.text: What is a primary cause of 'peak tailing' in a gas chromatogram?
options: A. Using an excessively fast carrier gas flow rate
B. Active adsorption sites (such as silanol groups) on the column wall, column overloading, or dead volume
C. Operating the oven at a constant isothermal temperature
D. Using helium as a carrier gas instead of nitrogen

TOS5_Section2.text: What phenomenon is indicated by a gradually rising baseline accompanied by baseline noise during high-temperature programmed GC runs?
options: A. Column bleed (loss of stationary phase degradation products at elevated temperatures)
B. Complete exhaustion of the carrier gas cylinder
C. Air leakage into the electron capture detector
D. Water condensation inside the injection port septum

TOS5_Section2.text: Why is an 'internal standard calibration method' superior to external standard calibration for quantitative GC analysis?
options: A. Internal standards eliminate the need for any reference compounds.
B. Adding a fixed amount of internal standard corrects for minor variations in manual injection volume and instrumental drift.
C. Internal standards make detectors infinitely sensitive.
D. External standards cannot be measured by peak area.

TOS5_Section2.text: What is the fundamental difference in sample capability between Gas Chromatography (GC) and High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (HPLC)?
options: A. GC requires volatile and thermally stable analytes with a gas mobile phase, whereas HPLC handles non-volatile, polar, or thermally unstable compounds with a liquid mobile phase.
B. GC can only analyze inorganic salts, while HPLC analyzes gases.
C. HPLC uses helium carrier gas at 300 psi.
D. There are no operational differences between GC and HPLC.

TOS5_Section2.text: What does the 'dead time' ($t_m$ or $t_0$) represent in gas chromatography?
options: A. The time required for the instrument to power down
B. The elution time of an unretained, non-interacting marker compound through the column
C. The total time spent heating the injection port
D. The half-life of the detector filament

TOS5_Section2.text: What are 'ghost peaks' in gas chromatography?
options: A. Peaks representing radioactive decay products
B. Spurious peaks resulting from system contamination, septum bleed, or carryover from a previous injection
C. Negative peaks caused by air bubbles in the detector
D. Theoretical plates calculated by software

TOS5_Section2.text: When using hydrogen gas as a carrier gas in GC, what critical safety precaution must be strictly maintained?
options: A. Hydrogen lines must be operated above 500 psi.
B. Rigorous leak-testing must be performed regularly because hydrogen forms explosive mixtures with air.
C. Hydrogen must be mixed with 50% carbon dioxide.
D. The column oven door must remain wide open during analysis.

TOS5_Section2.text: According to the 'like dissolves like' principle in GC stationary phase selection, how should a polar stationary phase column be used?
options: A. To analyze nonpolar saturated alkanes exclusively
B. To effectively retain and separate polar analytes (such as alcohols and amines) through dipole-dipole or hydrogen-bonding interactions
C. To prevent all compounds from eluting
D. To convert polar compounds into halogenated derivatives

TOS6_Section1.text: What wavelength range is typically covered by ultraviolet (UV) spectroscopy in organic analysis?
options: A. 10 to 100 nm
B. 200 to 400 nm
C. 400 to 700 nm

TOS6_Section1.text: Which electronic transitions fall within the standard 200 to 800 nm UV-Vis spectral region for most organic molecules?
options: A. \sigma \rightarrow \sigma^* and n \rightarrow \sigma^*
B. \pi \rightarrow \pi^* and n \rightarrow \pi^*
C. Core electron shell excitation
D. Spin-flip nuclear magnetic resonance

TOS6_Section1.text: What is defined as a functional group or structural moiety within a molecule that absorbs light (e.g., C=C, C=O, aromatic rings)?
options: A. Auxochrome
B. Chromophore
C. Free radical
D. Chiral center

TOS6_Section1.text: What role does an auxochrome (such as -OH or -NH₂) play when attached to a chromophore?
options: A. It absorbs light strongly below 200 nm by itself and destroys the chromophore.
B. It does not absorb strongly on its own, but shifts or intensifies the absorption wavelength of the chromophore.
C. It converts organic compounds into inorganic salts.
D. It eliminates all electronic transitions.

TOS6_Section1.text: How does extended conjugation in a polyene system affect its absorption maximum ($\lambda_{max}$)?
options: A. It shifts absorption to a shorter wavelength (higher energy).
B. It shifts absorption to a longer wavelength (lower energy / smaller energy gap).
C. It eliminates absorption entirely.
D. It shifts absorption into the X-ray region.

TOS6_Section1.text: What term describes a bathochromic shift in UV-Vis spectroscopy?
options: A. A red shift toward a longer wavelength
B. A blue shift toward a shorter wavelength
C. An increase in transmittance percentage
D. A decrease in molar absorptivity

TOS6_Section1.text: According to the Beer-Lambert law ($A = \varepsilon b c$), what does the symbol $\varepsilon$ represent?
options: A. Optical path length in cm
B. Molar absorptivity (molar extinction coefficient)
C. Percent transmittance
D. Frequency of incident light

TOS6_Section1.text: If a chemical solution exhibits a Percent Transmittance (%T) of 10%, what is its calculated Absorbance (A)?
Which lamp source is required to provide continuous ultraviolet radiation in a UV-Vis spectrophotometer?
options: A. Tungsten-halogen lamp
B. Deuterium (or hydrogen) arc lamp
C. Sodium vapor lamp
D. Carbon-zinc dry cell

TOS6_Section1.text: Which cuvette material must be used when recording absorption spectra in the UV region (below 350 nm)?
options: A. Ordinary optical window glass
B. Standard polystyrene plastic
C. Quartz or fused silica
D. Soft lead glass

TOS6_Section1.text: Why must solvents like acetone or toluene be avoided when preparing samples for UV spectroscopy?
options: A. They react violently with quartz cuvettes.
B. They absorb strongly in the ultraviolet region, masking the analyte's peaks.
C. They cause immediate precipitation of the solute.
D. They are completely insoluble in water.

TOS6_Section1.text: What is the primary function of measuring a 'blank' solution (pure solvent) before reading samples in a spectrophotometer?
options: A. To calibrate the temperature of the sample compartment
B. To zero the instrument, compensating for solvent absorption and cuvette reflection/scattering
C. To precipitate out interfering inorganic ions
D. To clean the internal monochromator grating

TOS6_Section1.text: At what wavelength is quantitative absorbance measurements ideally performed to ensure maximum sensitivity and minimal analytical error?
options: A. Exactly 500 nm
B. At the wavelength of maximum absorbance ($\lambda_{max}$)
C. At the lowest possible UV cutoff wavelength
D. At 0 nm

TOS6_Section1.text: What common factor causes deviations from Beer's law at high analyte concentrations (typically when absorbance exceeds 1.0 to 1.5)?
options: A. Solute-solute intermolecular interactions, association/dissociation equilibria, and stray light
B. Complete freezing of the solvent molecules
C. Zero path length in the cuvette
D. Infinite expansion of molar absorptivity

TOS6_Section1.text: If a colored chemical solution absorbs light strongly in the blue region of the spectrum, what apparent color will it appear to human eyes?
options: A. Pure blue
B. Yellow-orange (complementary color)
C. Deep violet
D. Pitch black

TOS6_Section1.text: What term describes a hypsochromic shift in absorption?
options: A. A shift toward a longer wavelength (red shift)
B. A shift toward a shorter wavelength (blue shift)
C. An increase in peak absorbance intensity
D. A broadening of the absorption band

TOS6_Section1.text: What is the correct sequential order of components along the optical light path of a standard single-beam spectrophotometer?
options: A. Detector -> Sample -> Monochromator -> Light Source
B. Light Source -> Monochromator -> Sample Cuvette -> Detector -> Readout
C. Sample -> Light Source -> Detector -> Monochromator
D. Readout -> Detector -> Light Source -> Sample

TOS6_Section1.text: How should optical cuvettes be handled correctly during sample loading and placement into the spectrophotometer?
options: A. Held firmly by the clear optical window faces with bare fingers
B. Handled exclusively by the frosted side walls, wiping clear faces with lens paper
C. Dropped directly into the sample holder from a height
D. Cleaned with abrasive steel wool before each reading

TOS6_Section1.text: Which electronic transition requires the highest energy photons and appears at the shortest vacuum-UV wavelengths (below 200 nm)?
options: A. \sigma \rightarrow \sigma^*
B. n \rightarrow \pi^*
C. \pi \rightarrow \pi^*
D. d \rightarrow d transition

TOS6_Section1.text: What is considered the optimal, most accurate absorbance range for quantitative spectrophotometric analysis?
options: D. Above 3.00

TOS6_Section2.text: What physical phenomenon does infrared (IR) spectroscopy measure when interacting with a molecule?
options: A. Excitation of valence electrons to higher energy orbitals
B. Changes in molecular vibrations (stretching and bending modes)
C. Nuclear spin-flips in a magnetic field
D. Total molecular fragmentation and ionization

TOS6_Section2.text:
How are wavenumbers ($	ilde{
u}$) in units of cm⁻¹ mathematically related to the frequency and energy of infrared radiation?
options: A. Wavenumbers are inversely proportional to energy.
B. Higher wavenumber corresponds to higher frequency and higher energy.
C. Wavenumbers measure the absolute mass of the molecule.
D. Wavenumbers have no direct relation to light frequency.

TOS6_Section2.text: What fundamental selection rule governs whether a particular molecular vibration is active in the infrared spectrum?
options: A. The vibration must involve a net change in molecular dipole moment during the vibration.
B. The molecule must be a homonuclear diatomic gas like $N_2$ or $O_2$.
C. The molecule must absorb visible light simultaneously.
D. The dipole moment must remain strictly zero at all times.

TOS6_Section2.text: In an IR spectrum, approximately where is the characteristic diagnostic functional group region located?
options: A. 400 to 400ynth cm⁻¹
C. 1500 to 400 cm⁻¹

TOS6_Section2.text: Which characteristic absorption band in the IR spectrum indicates the presence of a hydrogen-bonded alcohol or phenol O-H stretch?
options: A. Sharp peak at 2250 cm⁻¹
B. Broad, strong band around 3200 to 3600 cm⁻¹
C. Sharp doublet at 1600 cm⁻¹
D. Very weak peak at 700 cm⁻¹

TOS6_Section2.text: What distinguishes the appearance of a carboxylic acid O-H stretch from an alcohol O-H stretch in an IR spectrum?
options: A. Carboxylic acid O-H is very broad (2500–3300 cm⁻¹) and often overlaps the C-H stretching region.
B. Carboxylic acid O-H appears as a sharp singlet at 4000 cm⁻¹.
C. Carboxylic acid O-H is completely invisible in IR.
D. Carboxylic acid O-H appears above 3800 cm⁻¹.

TOS6_Section2.text: How can primary, secondary, and tertiary amines be distinguished by their N-H stretching absorptions in the 3300 to 3500 cm⁻¹ region?
options: A. Primary shows two bands (doublet), secondary shows one band (singlet), and tertiary shows no N-H band.
B. Tertiary shows three bands, while primary shows none.
C. All amines show identical single peaks at 1710 cm⁻¹.
D. Amines do not absorb infrared radiation.

TOS6_Section2.text: What approximate wavenumber range corresponds to the highly diagnostic carbonyl (C=O) stretching absorption?
options: D. 600 to 800 cm⁻¹

TOS6_Section2.text: How does electronic conjugation with a double bond or aromatic ring affect the stretching frequency of a neighboring carbonyl (C=O) group?
options: A. It raises the C=O frequency by 100 cm⁻¹.
B. It lowers the C=O stretching frequency by roughly 20 to 30 cm⁻¹ due to increased single-bond character.
C. It shifts the C=O peak into the fingerprint region.
D. It eliminates the C=O peak entirely.

TOS6_Section2.text: Which functional group class exhibits two characteristic weak C-H stretching bands around 2720 and 2820 cm⁻¹ on the right side of the sp³ C-H stretch?
options: A. Ketones
B. Esters
C. Aldehydes
D. Alkynes

TOS6_Section2.text: Why must water and aqueous solutions NEVER be used with sodium chloride (NaCl) or potassium bromide (KBr) IR sample plates?
options: A. Water turns NaCl plates bright red.
B. Water dissolves the ionic salt plates instantly, and water absorbs strongly in the IR region.
C. Water reacts with NaCl to form chlorine gas.
D. Water coats the plates with a non-removable polymer.

TOS6_Section2.text: What is the primary advantage of Fourier Transform Infrared (FTIR) spectrometers over older dispersive IR instruments?
options: A. FTIR uses a Michelson interferometer and computer to collect all wavelengths simultaneously, providing faster scans with higher signal-to-noise ratio.
B. FTIR requires radioactive carbon sources.
C. FTIR can only analyze solid samples in water.
D. FTIR eliminates the need for any background scan.

TOS6_Section2.text: When preparing a solid sample as a Nujol mull, why is it impossible to reliably identify alkane C-H stretching peaks in the sample?
options: A. Nujol is pure mineral oil (a saturated alkane), which produces heavy absorption bands in the exact same C-H region (2850–2950 cm⁻¹).
B. Nujol dissolves the sample completely into a gas.
C. Nujol reacts with the salt plates to form an opaque crust.
D. Nujol absorbs all light below 400 cm⁻¹.

TOS6_Section2.text: What is the purpose of running a background scan prior to acquiring an FTIR sample spectrum?
options: A. To measure room temperature
B. To measure and subtract the absorption contributions of atmospheric moisture (water vapor) and carbon dioxide ($CO_2$)
C. To calibrate the sample mass on a balance
D. To reset the interferometer mirror to zero

TOS6_Section2.text: Which molecule is completely IR-INACTIVE because its symmetrical stretching vibration produces zero net change in dipole moment?
options: A. Carbon monoxide (CO)
B. Hydrogen chloride (HCl)
C. Nitrogen gas ($N_2$, homonuclear diatomic)
D. Acetone ($CH_3COCH_3$)

TOS6_Section2.text: What is the primary role of the 'fingerprint region' (approx. 1500 to 400 cm⁻¹) in an IR spectrum?
options: A. Identifying the molecular mass precisely
B. Providing a complex, unique spectral pattern used to confirm molecular identity by direct reference matching
C. Measuring melting point depression
D. Detecting inorganic heavy metal cations

TOS6_Section2.text: Why must KBr (potassium bromide) used for making pressed IR pellets be thoroughly dried and handled carefully?
options: A. Wet KBr explodes under hydraulic pressure.
B. KBr is extremely hygroscopic and absorbed moisture introduces broad interfering O-H peaks around 3400 cm⁻¹.
C. Dry KBr is highly flammable.
D. Moisture converts KBr into liquid bromine.

TOS6_Section2.text: Rank the following carbonyl stretching frequencies (C=O) from HIGHEST wavenumber to LOWEST wavenumber:
options: A. Amide > Ketone > Ester > Acid chloride
B. Acid chloride (~1800) > Ester (~1740) > Ketone (~1715) > Amide (~1680)
C. Ketone > Amide > Acid chloride > Ester
D. Ester > Acid chloride > Amide > Ketone

TOS6_Section2.text: What is the fundamental spectroscopic technique used in an Attenuated Total Reflectance (ATR) accessory for IR analysis?
options: A. Total internal reflection of an IR beam through a high-refractive-index crystal where an evanescent wave interacts directly with pressed sample contact.
B. Transmission of IR light through 10 meters of liquid gas.
C. Scattering of monochromatic X-rays off crystal planes.
D. Laser ablation of solid powders.

TOS6_Section2.text: What structural feature gives rise to sharp, strong C≡N (nitrile) stretching absorptions appearing near 2210 to 2260 cm⁻¹?
options: A. A carbon-nitrogen triple bond with strong dipole moment change
B. A carbon-oxygen single bond in a ring
C. A symmetrical aromatic ring vibration
D. An isolated quaternary ammonium ion

TOS7_Section1.text: What is the primary rationale for segregating laboratory chemical wastes by hazard category?
options: A. To make waste containers heavier and easier to transport
B. To prevent dangerous exothermic or gas-evolving reactions between incompatible wastes and lower overall disposal costs
C. To allow all waste to be poured down the municipal sewer system safely
D. To eliminate the need for container labeling

TOS7_Section1.text: Which four core characteristics define hazardous waste under standard regulatory classifications?
options: A. Sweet, sour, salty, and bitter
B. Ignitable, corrosive, reactive, and toxic
C. Transparent, dense, volatile, and viscous
D. Metallic, organic, aqueous, and solid

TOS7_Section1.text: Why must halogenated organic solvents (e.g., dichloromethane, chloroform) be strictly segregated from non-halogenated organic solvents (e.g., acetone, hexane)?
options: A. Halogenated solvents freeze solid at room temperature.
B. Halogenated solvents require specialized high-temperature incineration to prevent dangerous acid gas and dioxin emissions and are more costly to dispose of.
C. Halogenated solvents react with glass to form permanent gels.
D. Mixing them causes an immediate explosion.

TOS7_Section1.text: What happens if even a small volume of a halogenated solvent is mixed into a drum of non-halogenated organic solvent waste?
options: A. The entire drum must be reclassified and disposed of as more expensive halogenated waste.
B. The solvents automatically neutralize each other into pure water.
C. The mixture becomes non-hazardous and can be poured down the drain.
D. The volume doubles instantly.

TOS7_Section1.text: Why must cyanide-containing or sulfide-containing aqueous wastes be kept strictly alkaline and separated from acidic waste streams?
options: A. Acidification releases extremely toxic hydrogen cyanide (HCN) or hydrogen sulfide (H₂S) gases.
B. Acids cause cyanide solutions to crystallize into solid diamonds.
C. Alkalinity prevents cyanide from dissolving in water.
D. Acids turn cyanide into harmless table salt.

TOS7_Section1.text: How should chemical oxidizers (such as nitrates, perchlorates, permanganates, and peroxides) be stored and managed relative to organic compounds?
options: A. Mixed directly with organic solvents to stabilize them
B. Stored strictly separate from organics and reducing agents to prevent fire or explosion
C. Used as daily cleaning solutions for lab benches
D. Stored in unsealed open containers

TOS7_Section1.text: What primary hazard is associated with old, opened containers of liquid ethers (like diethyl ether or THF) left sitting on a shelf?
options: A. They absorb nitrogen gas and turn blue.
B. They form shock-sensitive, potentially explosive organic peroxides over time.
C. They spontaneously freeze into hard plastics.
D. They lose all chemical reactivity instantly.

TOS7_Section1.text: Where should chemically contaminated solid items such as used filter paper, silica gel, drying agents, and contaminated gloves be disposed of?
options: A. Ordinary municipal paper trash bins
B. Dedicated solid chemical waste containers
C. Down the sink with warm tap water
D. Recycled as clean office paper

TOS7_Section1.text: What is the correct procedure for handling an unknown, unlabeled chemical discovered in a fume hood?
options: A. Pour it down the sink drain with plenty of water.
B. Mix it into the general organic waste carboy.
C. Treat it as hazardous waste, never mix it, label it clearly as an 'unknown', and identify it before disposal.
D. Evaporate it rapidly using a heat gun.

TOS7_Section1.text: What hazard arises when strong acids and strong bases are inadvertently mixed together in an unmanaged container?
options: A. A violent, highly exothermic neutralization reaction that can cause boiling and splattering
B. Total freezing of the liquid mixture
C. Complete conversion into unreactive carbon dioxide gas
D. Generation of pure electrical current

TOS7_Section1.text: What toxic gas is produced when household bleach (sodium hypochlorite solution) is accidentally mixed with an acid or an ammonia-containing cleaning product?
options: A. Carbon monoxide or carbon dioxide
B. Chlorine gas ($Cl_2$) or toxic chloramine vapors
C. Pure oxygen gas
D. Nitrogen trifluoride

TOS7_Section1.text: Why is it dangerous to store corrosive acidic waste solutions in metal cans or drums?
options: A. Acids dissolve the metal, causing container leaks and generating flammable hydrogen gas.
B. Metal turns acids into solid crystals.
C. Acids make metal magnetic.
D. Metal neutralizes acids instantly.

TOS7_Section1.text: What material is generally recommended for manufacturing waste carboys and containers holding aqueous acids or bases?
options: A. Thin sheet aluminum
B. High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) or approved chemical-resistant polymers
C. Untreated paperboard
D. Ordinary food-grade cardboard

TOS7_Section1.text: To what maximum level should liquid hazardous waste carboys be filled to allow adequate safety headspace for thermal expansion and vapor pressure?
options: A. 100% full right up to the threads
B. Typically 75% to 90% full (leaving proper headspace)
C. Exactly 20% full
D. Headspace is unnecessary for liquid wastes.

TOS7_Section1.text: Which information must be explicitly displayed on a hazardous waste container label in a chemical laboratory?
options: A. Market retail price and supplier catalog number
B. The words 'Hazardous Waste', full chemical names (no formulas/abbreviations), approximate percentages, and start date
C. Instructor's home telephone number
D. Molecular weight and boiling point only

TOS7_Section1.text: What is the purpose of placing hazardous waste containers inside secondary containment trays or tubs?
options: A. To catch and contain any leaks or spills from the primary container and segregate incompatible chemical classes
B. To heat the waste to boiling
C. To weigh the waste automatically
D. To insulate the waste from room lighting

TOS7_Section1.text: How should broken glass contaminated with hazardous chemicals be discarded?
options: A. Thrown into regular black plastic trash bags
B. Placed into a dedicated, puncture-resistant rigid container specifically labeled for chemically contaminated broken glass
C. Swept under the lab bench
D. Washed in the sink and put back in glassware drawers

TOS7_Section1.text: What reaction occurs when concentrated nitric acid is mixed with common organic solvents like acetone or ethanol?
options: A. A violent, potentially explosive oxidation-reduction reaction
B. Formation of a stable cooling solution
C. Dilution into harmless soap
D. Complete polymerization into solid plastic

TOS7_Section1.text: How should heavy-metal waste solutions containing mercury, lead, cadmium, or chromium be handled?
options: A. Diluted with tap water and poured down the sink
B. Collected separately in dedicated hazardous metal waste streams and never poured down the drain
C. Evaporated to dryness in an open evaporating dish on the bench
D. Mixed with organic solvents for fuel blending

TOS7_Section1.text: What safety practice must be maintained regarding funnels used to pour liquid waste into a carboy?
options: A. Leave the funnel resting in the carboy opening permanently so anyone can dump waste at any time.
B. Remove the funnel immediately after pouring and secure the container cap tightly closed.
C. Seal the top of the funnel with electrical tape.
D. Heat the funnel with a Bunsen burner to evaporate drips.

TOS7_Section2.text: According to the waste minimization hierarchy, what is the most preferred and effective strategy for managing laboratory chemical waste?
options: A. Incineration at high temperatures
B. Source reduction (minimizing waste generation at the source by scaling down or substituting chemicals)
C. Deep-well underground injection
D. Dilution and discharge into municipal sewage systems

TOS7_Section2.text: Which section of a standard Safety Data Sheet (SDS) specifically provides guidance and considerations regarding safe waste disposal practices?
options: A. Section 2: Hazard Identification
B. Section 8: Exposure Controls/Personal Protection
C. Section 13: Disposal Considerations
D. Section 16: Other Information

TOS7_Section2.text: What principle governs the legal concept that a waste generator remains legally responsible for the proper handling, transport, treatment, and ultimate disposal of their hazardous waste from 'cradle to grave'?
options: A. Strict generator liability and cradle-to-grave responsibility
B. The statute of limitations on chemical synthesis
C. Municipal immunity from environmental liability
D. The doctrine of accidental release absorption

TOS7_Section2.text: Which condition must be met for an aqueous chemical solution to be considered potentially acceptable for drain disposal (where locally permitted)?
options: A. It must contain high concentrations of heavy metals like lead and mercury.
B. It must be dilute, non-toxic, non-flammable, non-reactive, water-soluble, and neutralized to an acceptable pH range (typically 6 to 9).
C. It must consist entirely of concentrated organic solvents.
D. It must release pungent toxic gases upon contact with water.

TOS7_Section2.text: How should a strong, concentrated mineral acid solution be safely treated prior to neutral disposal or management?
options: A. Pour water rapidly directly into the concentrated acid container.
B. Slowly add the acid into a large volume of cold water with stirring, then cautiously neutralize with a weak base like sodium bicarbonate.
C. Mix the acid directly with concentrated sodium cyanide solution.
D. Evaporate the acid on an open Bunsen burner flame.

TOS7_Section2.text: What chemical treatment is necessary when handling aqueous waste streams containing toxic Hexavalent Chromium [Cr(VI)] before final precipitation?
options: A. Reduce Cr(VI) to Cr(III) using a reducing agent like sodium bisulfite under acidic conditions, followed by hydroxide precipitation.
B. Expose the solution to direct sunlight to evaporate the chromium atoms.
C. Add concentrated ammonium hydroxide to form explosive complexes.
D. Heat the solution to 1000 °C without chemical additives.

TOS7_Section2.text: What is the proper method for cleaning up and managing a small spill of liquid elemental mercury ($Hg$) in the laboratory?
options: A. Vacuum it up using a standard laboratory vacuum cleaner with a cloth bag.
B. Sweep it up with a stiff broom to aerosolize droplets for quick evaporation.
C. Use specialized mercury spill kits, aspirator bulbs, or zinc/sulfur powder to amalgamate and contain droplets securely.
D. Flush the mercury down the nearest floor drain with hot water.

TOS7_Section2.text: Why must halogenated organic waste solvents be incinerated in specialized high-tech facilities equipped with scrubbers?
options: A. To generate electricity for the laboratory building
B. To capture corrosive acid gases (like HCl) and prevent the formation of toxic dioxins released by incomplete halogen combustion
C. To convert halogenated compounds into edible salts
D. To lower the operating temperature of the furnace below 200 °C

TOS7_Section2.text: Under Philippine law, which primary national legislation enacted in 1990 serves as the comprehensive legal framework for controlling toxic substances and hazardous and nuclear wastes?
options: A. Republic Act No. 6969 (Toxic Substances and Hazardous and Nuclear Wastes Control Act of 1990)
B. Republic Act No. 9003 (Ecological Solid Waste Management Act)
C. Republic Act No. 8749 (Philippine Clean Air Act of 1999)
D. Republic Act No. 9275 (Philippine Clean Water Act of 2004)

TOS7_Section2.text: Which government agency is designated under Philippine law (such as RA 6969) as the primary implementing agency tasked with regulating chemicals and hazardous wastes?
options: A. Department of Health (DOH)
B. Department of Environment and Natural Resources (DENR)
C. Department of Energy (DOE)
D. Department of Trade and Industry (DTI)

TOS7_Section2.text: What does DENR Administrative Order (DAO) No. 2013-22 primarily govern regarding hazardous materials in the Philippines?
options: A. Revised procedures and standards for the management, generation, transport, storage, and treatment of hazardous wastes
B. National standards for potable drinking water purity
C. Rules for commercial fishing in municipal waters
D. Guidelines for highway vehicle emission testing

TOS7_Section2.text: What is the correct protocol for handling and discarding empty reagent bottles that previously held non-acutely toxic chemicals?
options: A. Smash the glass bottles immediately on the floor to prevent reuse.
B. Triple-rinse the container with an appropriate solvent (adding rinsate to proper waste), deface the label, and recycle or discard per facility rules.
C. Fill the empty bottle with concentrated nitric acid and leave it uncapped.
D. Throw them directly into municipal food waste bins.

TOS7_Section2.text: How should empty high-pressure gas cylinders (e.g., nitrogen or argon) be managed when they are fully depleted?
options: A. Cut the metal body in half using a hacksaw.
B. Leave them open in the hallway with the valves removed.
C. Secure the valve safety cap, label them empty, and return them directly to the industrial gas supplier.
D. Bury them in the facility's back garden.

TOS7_Section2.text: What is the initial immediate response step when a chemical spill occurs in the laboratory?
options: A. Ignore the spill and continue working until the shift ends.
B. Alert nearby personnel, assess the hazard, evacuate the immediate area if dangerous, and don appropriate PPE before containment.
C. Pour water over all organic solvent spills regardless of identity.
D. Turn off all room lights and lock the laboratory doors from the outside.

TOS7_Section2.text: Why is allowing volatile organic hazardous waste solvents to 'evaporate away' inside a fume hood strictly prohibited as a disposal method?
options: A. Evaporation takes too many days to complete.
B. It causes atmospheric air pollution, violates environmental protection laws, and creates fire/explosion hazards in ductwork.
C. Evaporation turns organic solvents into solid gold.
D. Fume hood blowers run on high-voltage direct current.

TOS7_Section2.text: What specific treatment approach is used to destroy aqueous cyanide waste streams safely?
options: A. Alkaline chlorination (oxidizing cyanide using hypochlorite at high pH under strict supervision)
B. Direct acidification with concentrated hydrochloric acid
C. Boiling the solution down to dryness in an open beaker
D. Freezing the liquid with dry ice

TOS7_Section2.text: What is the primary function of a hazardous waste manifest or waste transport record in regulatory compliance?
options: A. To serve as a decorative poster on laboratory walls
B. To provide a formal, traceable chain-of-custody document tracking waste from generator to transport and ultimate TSD facility treatment
C. To calculate employee salary deductions
D. To list chemical formulas for undergraduate examinations

TOS7_Section2.text: Which disposal destination is appropriate for non-halogenated flammable waste solvents that cannot be recycled in-house?
options: A. Industrial fuel blending for cement kilns or high-efficiency incineration
B. Municipal storm drains
C. Ordinary paper recycling plants
D. Deep-sea ocean dumping

TOS7_Section2.text: What physical form do heavy-metal sludge residues typically take when prepared for final disposal in an engineered secure landfill?
options: A. Highly volatile toxic gases
B. Stabilized, chemically solidified solid monoliths that resist leaching
C. Low-viscosity liquid suspensions
D. Pure crystalline metallic powder

TOS7_Section2.text: Which waste minimization practice involves redesigning experimental procedures to utilize milligram quantities instead of multi-gram quantities of reagents?
options: A. Microscale experimentation
B. Macroscale synthesis overload
C. Solvent evaporation acceleration
D. Infinite dilution analysis

TOS8_Section1.text: What is the fundamental difference between chemical 'toxicity', 'hazard', and 'risk'?
options: A. Toxicity is the likelihood of exposure, hazard is cost, and risk is temperature.
B. Toxicity is the inherent harmful capacity of a substance, hazard is its potential to cause harm under specific conditions, and risk is the actual probability of harm occurring given exposure.
C. Toxicity and hazard mean the exact same thing as risk.
D. Risk is fixed and independent of exposure levels.

TOS8_Section1.text: What does a lower $LD_{50}$ (Lethal Dose 50) value indicate about a chemical substance?
options: A. The substance has very low toxicity and requires massive doses to cause harm.
B. The substance has higher toxicity, meaning a smaller dose is required to kill 50% of the test population.
C. The substance is completely non-hazardous and safe for drain disposal.
D. $LD_{50}$ measures boiling point volatility, not toxicity.

TOS8_Section1.text: Which exposure route is statistically the most common pathway for accidental chemical absorption in laboratory environments?
options: A. Intravenous injection
B. Inhalation of vapors, mists, or dusts
C. Direct ingestion via food
D. Absorption through fingernails

TOS8_Section1.text: What does the Threshold Limit Value - Time-Weighted Average (TLV-TWA) represent in occupational health?
options: A. The absolute ceiling concentration that must never be exceeded for even a second.
B. The time-weighted average concentration for a normal 8-hour workday and 40-hour workweek to which nearly all workers may be repeatedly exposed without adverse effect.
C. The total weight of chemical required to cause a fire.
D. The maximum lethal dose for 100% of animals.

TOS8_Section1.text: Which common organic solvent is notoriously metabolized in the human body to formaldehyde and formic acid, causing severe metabolic acidosis and permanent blindness via optic nerve damage?
options: A. Ethanol
B. Methanol
C. Isopropanol
D. Acetone

TOS8_Section1.text: What chronic medical condition is classically associated with occupational or long-term exposure to benzene vapor?
options: A. Bone marrow toxicity and acute myeloid leukemia (known human carcinogen)
B. Permanent color blindness
C. Chronic kidney stones
D. Enhanced skeletal muscle growth

TOS8_Section1.text: Chronic exposure to which aliphatic hydrocarbon solvent causes peripheral neuropathy (progressive nerve damage and muscle weakness in the extremities)?
options: A. Methane
B. n-Hexane
C. Cyclohexane
D. Propane

TOS8_Section1.text: What hazardous degradation product is slowly formed when chloroform ($CHCl_3$) is exposed to atmospheric oxygen and light?
options: A. Phosgene gas ($COCl_2$)
B. Carbon dioxide ($CO_2$)
C. Methane gas ($CH_4$)
D. Ethyl chloride

TOS8_Section1.text: Why is phenol particularly treacherous when spilled on human skin?
options: A. It freezes skin instantly into ice.
B. It acts as a local anesthetic, deadening pain receptors so severe chemical burns occur without immediate pain sensation before rapid systemic absorption.
C. It turns skin bright neon green.
D. It is completely insoluble in water and biological tissue.

TOS8_Section1.text: Which toxic condition is caused by aromatic amines (like aniline or nitrobenzene) reacting with hemoglobin in the blood, impairing oxygen transport and turning skin and lips a characteristic bluish color?
options: A. Methemoglobinemia
B. Hyperglycemia
C. Leukemia
D. Scurvy

TOS8_Section1.text: What is the primary toxicological hazard associated with the ingestion of ethylene glycol (the primary component of automotive antifreeze)?
options: A. Immediate hair loss
B. Severe metabolic acidosis and acute kidney failure due to toxic oxalate crystal precipitation
C. Permanent hearing loss
D. Rapid weight gain

TOS8_Section1.text: Why is human olfactory sense (smell) considered an UNRELIABLE and dangerous indicator of chemical safety or vapor presence?
options: A. All chemicals smell pleasant.
B. Some toxic gases cause olfactory fatigue (desensitization of nasal nerves like $H_2S$), while others have odor thresholds well above safe exposure limits.
C. Human noses cannot detect organic molecules.
D. Odors travel faster than air molecules.

TOS8_Section1.text: What toxicological classification is assigned to carbon monoxide ($CO$) and hydrogen cyanide ($HCN$) because they disrupt cellular oxygen utilization?
options: A. Chemical asphyxiants
B. Simple irritants
C. Optical sensitizers
D. Alkaline buffers

TOS8_Section1.text: What exposure limit is defined as 'Immediately Dangerous to Life or Health' (IDLH)?
options: A. The concentration that causes minor skin irritation after 8 hours.
B. A concentration posing an immediate threat of death, irreversible adverse health effects, or impaired ability to escape.
C. The lowest detectable odor threshold.
D. The maximum flammable range limit.

TOS8_Section1.text: Which heavy metal exists as a room-temperature liquid and poses a severe chronic neurotoxic vapor hazard if spilled or left uncontained?
options: A. Iron
B. Mercury ($Hg$)
C. Copper
D. Zinc

TOS8_Section1.text: What is a major toxicological concern regarding dichloromethane (methylene chloride, $CH_2Cl_2$) when inhaled in poorly ventilated spaces?
options: A. It polymerizes into solid rubber inside the lungs.
B. It acts as a CNS depressant and is metabolized in the body to carbon monoxide, elevating carboxyhemoglobin levels in the blood.
C. It converts instantly into drinking water.
D. It neutralizes stomach acid.

TOS8_Section1.text: How do acute exposure effects differ fundamentally from chronic exposure effects?
options: A. Acute effects result from single or short-term high exposures with rapid onset, whereas chronic effects result from repeated, long-term low-level exposures with delayed onset.
B. Acute effects only occur in animals, while chronic effects occur in humans.
C. Acute effects are beneficial to health, while chronic effects are neutral.
D. There is no biological difference between them.

TOS8_Section1.text: What is the toxicological significance of acetonitrile ($CH_3CN$) compared to many other simple organic solvents?
options: A. It is completely inert and non-toxic like water.
B. It is metabolized in vivo to release toxic cyanide ions ($CN^-$), posing systemic poisoning risks upon skin absorption or ingestion.
C. It freezes at 50 °C.
D. It acts as a powerful vitamin supplement.

TOS8_Section1.text: What specialized exposure limit term defines a 15-minute time-weighted average exposure that should not be exceeded at any time during a workday?
options: A. Ceiling limit (C)
B. Short-Term Exposure Limit (STEL)
C. Lethal Concentration 50 ($LC_{50}$)
D. Baseline threshold

TOS8_Section1.text: What phenomenon occurs when two hazardous chemicals combined produce a biological health effect significantly greater than the simple sum of their individual effects (e.g., ethanol enhancing halogenated solvent toxicity)?
options: A. Synergism (synergistic effect)
B. Neutralization
C. Precipitation
D. Osmosis

TOS8_Section2.text: According to the industrial hygiene hierarchy of controls, what is the MOST effective method for controlling workplace and laboratory hazards?
options: A. Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)
B. Elimination (physically removing the hazard entirely)
C. Administrative controls and safety signs
D. Engineering controls like fume hoods

TOS8_Section2.text: Why is Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) always placed at the very bottom (least effective rank) of the hazard control hierarchy?
options: A. PPE is too expensive to purchase.
B. PPE does not eliminate or reduce the hazard itself; it relies entirely on human compliance and can fail or degrade upon exposure.
C. PPE is illegal to use in chemical laboratories.
D. PPE interferes with chemical weighing accuracy.

TOS8_Section2.text: What is the correct operational procedure when working with volatile toxic substances inside a chemical fume hood?
options: A. Fully open the sash to maximum height so you can lean your head inside.
B. Work at least 15 cm (6 inches) inside the hood sash, keep the sash at its designated working height, and avoid blocking airflow slots.
C. Turn off the exhaust fan to conserve electricity while working.
D. Store large equipment and chemical carboys permanently inside the hood.

TOS8_Section2.text: How should compressed gas cylinders be stored and secured safely in the laboratory at all times?
options: A. Laid flat on the floor in active walkways to save vertical space
B. Secured upright with sturdy chains or straps to a wall or bench, with safety valve caps in place when not in use
C. Locked inside wooden kitchen cabinets
D. Balanced loosely on top of chemical fume hoods

TOS8_Section2.text: What is the very FIRST step in conducting a comprehensive laboratory risk assessment before starting an unfamiliar or modified experiment?
options: A. Ordering expensive safety goggles
B. Identifying hazards (reviewing SDS, procedures, and potential risks)
C. Disposing of all hazardous waste in the building
D. Evacuating the entire building

TOS8_Section2.text: Which control measure exemplifies 'Substitution' in the hierarchy of controls when evaluating solvent toxicity?
options: A. Wearing thick rubber gloves
B. Replacing known human carcinogen benzene with less toxic toluene
C. Installing a new ventilation duct
D. Writing a mandatory Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

TOS8_Section2.text: Which chemical storage pairing represents a severe safety incompatibility that must be strictly segregated?
options: A. Storing water and glass beakers together
B. Storing strong oxidizing agents directly next to flammable organic solvents
C. Storing sodium chloride in a plastic jar
D. Storing ethanol and methanol in the same flammable cabinet

TOS8_Section2.text: Why is perchloric acid strictly prohibited from being used in standard laboratory fume hoods without a specialized washdown system?
options: A. Perchloric acid reacts with wood to make it turn purple.
B. Perchloric acid vapors react with metal ductwork to form shock-sensitive, highly explosive metal perchlorates that can detonate upon vibration.
C. Perchloric acid neutralizes all air currents instantly.
D. Perchloric acid freezes inside the blower fan.

TOS8_Section2.text: What safety precaution must be implemented when transferring flammable liquid solvents between two metal containers to prevent static electricity ignition?
options: A. Perform the transfer inside a dark room.
B. Ground and bond both metal containers together electrically.
C. Heat the solvent to 100 °C prior to pouring.
D. Wear woolen sweaters.

TOS8_Section2.text: What is the correct protocol for transporting heavy compressed gas cylinders across a facility corridor?
options: A. Roll the cylinder horizontally along the floor.
B. Carry the cylinder over your shoulder.
C. Use an approved dedicated cylinder cart with the cylinder securely strapped and valve safety caps screwed on.
D. Push the cylinder while it stands completely unsecured.

TOS8_Section2.text: What strict rule applies regarding working alone in an organic chemistry laboratory handling hazardous reagents?
options: A. Working alone is actively encouraged to improve personal focus.
B. Never work alone; a second person must always be present or within immediate contact in case of emergency.
C. You may work alone only if you wear two pairs of safety glasses.
D. Working alone is permitted during night hours only.

TOS8_Section2.text: How should large, heavy glass chemical bottles (e.g., 4-liter acid or solvent bottles) be stored on chemical storage shelving?
options: A. On the highest top shelf for easy visibility
B. On low shelves near the floor to minimize drop distances and tipping risks
C. Balanced on the edge of the sink
D. Suspended from ceiling hooks

TOS8_Section2.text: What appropriate personal protective equipment and handling precautions must be used when working with cryogenic liquids like liquid nitrogen?
options: A. Bare hands and unsealed airtight glass jugs
B. Insulated cryogenic gloves, face shield, eye protection, and containers that are never tightly sealed against pressure buildup
C. Cotton lab aprons and open sandals
D. Rubber dishwashing gloves

TOS8_Section2.text: Why must laboratory aisles, exits, and safety equipment access points (such as eyewash stations and fire extinguishers) remain completely unobstructed?
options: A. To ensure quick emergency evacuation and immediate access to safety gear during an incident
B. To make the laboratory look aesthetically pleasing
C. To prevent dust from settling on fire extinguishers
D. To comply with interior design regulations

TOS8_Section2.text: What key safety practice should be followed when executing a chemical reaction known to be moderately exothermic?
options: A. Add all reagents instantaneously and seal the vessel tightly.
B. Scale up gradually, add reagents slowly with stirring, and have an appropriate cooling bath prepared and ready.
C. Heat the reaction vessel with a direct blowtorch to drive completion.
D. Turn off all fume hood ventilation.

TOS8_Section2.text: What protective limitation applies to a standard chemical fume hood in terms of external lab safety?
options: A. A fume hood protects against chemical dust or hazardous exposures originating outside its sash in the open room.
B. A fume hood provides zero protection against chemical hazards or dust generated outside the hood in the general room environment.
C. A fume hood stops all ionizing radiation instantly.
D. A fume hood acts as a blast shelter for high-explosive detonations.

TOS8_Section2.text: Which option is an example of an 'Engineering Control' in laboratory safety management?
options: A. Posting a 'Wear Goggles' warning sign
B. Installing chemical fume hoods, safety shields, and automatic fire suppression systems
C. Establishing a written attendance policy
D. Requiring lab coats

TOS8_Section2.text: What rule governs leaving active heating apparatus or chemical reactions unattended in the laboratory?
options: A. Reactions may be left running unattended overnight without check.
B. Never leave active heating, refluxing, or hazardous chemical reactions unattended; establish monitoring protocols.
C. Unattended reactions proceed twice as fast.
D. Heating mantles turn off automatically after 10 seconds.

TOS8_Section2.text: What is the primary function of secondary containment trays (bunding) beneath stored chemical containers?
options: A. To catch and hold liquid leaks or spills, preventing intermixing of incompatible chemicals or escape into drains
B. To heat chemicals to boiling temperature
C. To measure the exact density of stored reagents
D. To filter air entering the container

TOS8_Section2.text: What does 'Administrative Controls' encompass in the safety hierarchy?
options: A. Physical ventilation fans and scrubbers
B. Standard operating procedures (SOPs), safety training, signage, labeling, and work scheduling rules
C. Chemical substitution of toxic reagents
D. Steel blast walls

TOS8_Section3.text: What three core elements compose the traditional fire triangle required to sustain combustion?
options: A. Water, nitrogen, and carbon
B. Fuel, oxygen, and heat
C. Acid, base, and salt
D. Pressure, volume, and temperature

TOS8_Section3.text: Which class of fire involves flammable liquids and gases such as laboratory organic solvents, gasoline, and oils?
options: A. Class A
B. Class B
C. Class C
D. Class D

TOS8_Section3.text: Why must water NEVER be used directly on a Class B flammable liquid solvent fire?
options: A. Water freezes instantly upon contact with solvents.
B. Water is denser than most organic solvents and causes the burning liquid to float and spread rapidly, intensifying the fire.
C. Water turns solvents into solid plastic.
D. Water reacts with solvents to produce electric shock.

TOS8_Section3.text: Which fire extinguisher type is ideal for electrical (Class C) and flammable liquid (Class B) fires because it leaves zero chemical residue, though it displaces oxygen in confined spaces?
options: A. Water stream extinguisher
B. Carbon dioxide ($CO_2$) extinguisher
C. Monoammonium phosphate dry chemical
D. Wet chemical extinguisher

TOS8_Section3.text: What do the letters in the acronym 'PASS' stand for when operating a portable fire extinguisher?
options: A. Press, Apply, Spray, Shield
B. Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep
C. Point, Activate, Smother, Stop
D. Protect, Alarm, Suppress, Save

TOS8_Section3.text: Under what specific conditions is it acceptable and safe for a laboratory worker to attempt fighting a small fire with a fire extinguisher?
options: A. Only if the fire is small, contained, you have the correct extinguisher, a clear exit behind you, and the alarm has been raised.
B. Whenever a smoke detector starts beeping.
C. If the fire involves combustible metals like magnesium.
D. If you are alone in the building at night.

TOS8_Section3.text: What does the acronym 'RACE' represent in emergency fire response procedures?
options: A. Run, Avoid, Call, Escape
B. Rescue, Alarm, Contain, Extinguish/Evacuate
C. Release, Absorb, Cool, Evacuate
D. React, Assess, Control, Exit

TOS8_Section3.text: What is the mandatory minimum duration for flushing chemical splashes out of the eyes at an emergency eyewash station?
options: A. Exactly 10 seconds
B. At least 15 minutes
C. 2 to 3 minutes
D. Until the water runs cold

TOS8_Section3.text: Why is it dangerous and strictly discouraged to apply chemical neutralizing solutions (e.g., weak acid for a base burn) directly to chemical burns or splashes on human skin?
options: A. Neutralization reactions are exothermic and release heat, causing thermal burns that worsen tissue damage.
B. Neutralizers turn skin bright blue.
C. Skin instantly dissolves chemical neutralizers.
D. Neutralizers cause immediate bone dissolution.

TOS8_Section3.text: What specific first-aid treatment is commonly recommended for phenol skin contact in many laboratory emergency protocols?
options: A. Rinsing with concentrated sulfuric acid
B. Wiping thoroughly with polyethylene glycol (PEG) or washing with copious water/soap, followed by immediate medical care
C. Applying hot vegetable oil
D. Sealing the burn with electrical tape

TOS8_Section3.text: What is the correct initial physical response if a worker's clothing accidentally catches fire in the laboratory?
options: A. Run as fast as possible toward the exit doors
B. Stop, drop, and roll, or wrap in a fire blanket or use a safety shower
C. Stand completely still and wait for assistance
D. Blow on the flames to cool them

TOS8_Section3.text: How can a small, contained fire inside a boiling flask or small beaker be extinguished quickly without discharging a fire extinguisher?
options: A. Pouring a beaker of water directly into the flask
B. Covering the opening with a watch glass, ceramic lid, or solid non-flammable object to smother the oxygen supply
C. Fanning the flames with a notebook
D. Blowing compressed air across the top

TOS8_Section3.text: Which class of fire involves burning combustible active metals such as magnesium, sodium, potassium, or lithium?
options: A. Class A
B. Class B
C. Class C
D. Class D

TOS8_Section3.text: During routine weekly inspections of stored-pressure fire extinguishers, what visual indicator confirms that the unit is fully pressurized and ready for use?
options: A. The pressure gauge needle is positioned firmly in the green operating zone.
B. The nozzle is plugged with cotton wool.
C. The metal cylinder feels ice cold.
D. The safety pin is completely removed.

TOS8_Section3.text: What critical rule must be followed if a chemical is accidentally swallowed in the laboratory?
options: A. Immediately induce vomiting by sticking fingers down the throat.
B. Call poison control or emergency services and do NOT induce vomiting unless explicitly instructed by the SDS or a medical professional.
C. Drink 2 liters of pure organic solvent to dilute it.
D. Take a nap until symptoms subside.

TOS8_Section3.text: How frequently are emergency eyewash stations typically tested and flushed under standard laboratory safety maintenance programs?
options: A. Once every decade
B. Weekly
C. Only after an accident occurs
D. Every leap year

TOS8_Section3.text: Which Philippine national law enacted in 2018 strengthens compliance with occupational safety and health standards (OHS) across all workplaces?
options: A. Republic Act No. 11058
B. Republic Act No. 6969
C. Republic Act No. 9003
D. Republic Act No. 8749

TOS8_Section3.text: Which national law governs fire prevention, protection, and safety code enforcement throughout the Philippines, administered by the Bureau of Fire Protection (BFP)?
options: A. Republic Act No. 9514 (Revised Fire Code of the Philippines)
B. Republic Act No. 9275 (Clean Water Act)
C. Republic Act No. 4166
D. Republic Act No. 7394

TOS8_Section3.text: Which Department Order issued by the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) contains the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of RA 11058?
options: A. DOLE Department Order No. 198-18
B. DOLE Department Order No. 57-04
C. DOLE Department Order No. 131-13
D. DOLE Department Order No. 18-A

TOS8_Section3.text: What is the designated nationwide emergency hotline telephone number in the Philippines?

TOS8_Section4.text: Where does Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) rank in the industrial hygiene hierarchy of controls?
options: A. The primary and most effective first line of defense
B. The absolute last line of defense when engineering and administrative controls cannot fully eliminate or reduce hazards
C. An optional accessory required only during guest visits
D. Equal in effectiveness to eliminating the hazard

TOS8_Section4.text: What is the minimum required eye protection for anyone entering an active chemical laboratory handling reagents?
options: A. Ordinary prescription reading glasses
B. Safety glasses with side shields
C. Tinted sunglasses
D. No eye protection is needed if looking away
