TOS8_Section4.text: When is the use of chemical splash goggles strictly required instead of standard safety glasses?
options: A. When handling liquids or corrosives with a risk of splashing into the eyes
B. Only when writing in a laboratory notebook
C. When operating an electronic digital balance
D. When walking through clean administrative hallways

TOS8_Section4.text: What is the correct protocol for wearing a full face shield in the chemical laboratory?
options: A. Worn alone without any safety glasses underneath
B. Worn over chemical splash goggles for severe splash or explosion hazards
C. Worn backward to protect the neck from drafts
D. Used only when looking through microscope lenses

TOS8_Section4.text: Which glove material is generally recommended for general-purpose laboratory use against weak acids, bases, and many oils, but has poor resistance to certain ketones and chlorinated solvents?
options: A. Nitrile
B. Viton
C. Butyl rubber
D. PVA (Polyvinyl alcohol)

TOS8_Section4.text: Why are standard latex disposable gloves discouraged or restricted for many organic chemistry laboratory applications?
options: A. Latex gloves dissolve instantly in water.
B. Latex offers poor chemical resistance to many organic solvents and poses severe latex protein allergy risks.
C. Latex makes fingers extremely magnetic.
D. Latex gloves conduct high-voltage electricity.

TOS8_Section4.text: Which glove material is specifically suited for handling aggressive aromatic and chlorinated solvents (such as benzene or dichloromethane)?
options: A. Thin natural latex
B. Viton (fluoroelastomer) or PVA
C. Cotton fabric
D. Ordinary polyethylene food wrap

TOS8_Section4.text: What is a major limitation of Polyvinyl Alcohol (PVA) gloves when used in aqueous chemical environments?
options: A. PVA dissolves in water.
B. PVA explodes upon contact with air.
C. PVA turns into solid glass when wet.
D. PVA is completely opaque.

TOS8_Section4.text: What fabric material is preferred for standard laboratory coats to prevent severe burn injuries during a fire?
options: A. 100% pure synthetic polyester or nylon
B. 100% heavy cotton or flame-resistant (FR) treated fabric
C. Thin plastic sheeting
D. Pure acrylic fibers

TOS8_Section4.text: Why are synthetic fabrics (like polyester or nylon) dangerous to wear near open flames or chemical fires in the lab?
options: A. They melt upon exposure to heat, adhering hot molten plastic directly to human skin and worsening burn severity.
B. They emit loud sirens when heated.
C. They attract static electricity that neutralizes acids.
D. They turn invisible in smoke.

TOS8_Section4.text: What footwear requirement is mandatory for all personnel working in an experimental chemistry laboratory?
options: A. Open-toe sandals to keep feet cool
B. Closed-toe, closed-heel shoes covering the entire foot, paired with long pants
C. Soft cloth bedroom slippers
D. Bare feet for better traction

TOS8_Section4.text: Which section of a standard Safety Data Sheet (SDS) provides specific guidance regarding recommended Personal Protective Equipment (PPE)?
options: A. Section 1: Identification
B. Section 8: Exposure Controls/Personal Protection
C. Section 13: Disposal Considerations
D. Section 14: Transport Information

TOS8_Section4.text: What is the critical function of an organic vapor cartridge on an Air-Purifying Respirator (APR)?
options: A. To filter and adsorb organic solvent vapors from inhaled air
B. To pump pure oxygen into the lungs from a compressed tank
C. To cool down room air before breathing
D. To amplify the wearer's voice

TOS8_Section4.text: What administrative and medical prerequisites must be met before an employee is permitted to wear a tight-fitting chemical respirator?
options: A. Medical clearance, professional fit-testing, and proper training
B. Paying a yearly licensing fee to the manufacturer
C. Growing a full beard to cushion the seal
D. No prerequisites are required

TOS8_Section4.text: How does facial hair (such as a beard or thick mustache) affect the performance of a tight-fitting respirator mask?
options: A. Facial hair improves the airtight seal by acting as a natural gasket.
B. Facial hair breaks the airtight seal along the sealing surface, allowing hazardous vapors or dust to leak inward.
C. Facial hair filters out all toxic gases automatically.
D. Facial hair has zero effect on respirator fit.

TOS8_Section4.text: Can a standard disposable paper dust mask or surgical mask be used as protection against toxic organic solvent vapors?
options: A. Yes, dust masks protect against all chemical hazards.
B. No, dust masks provide zero protection against chemical vapors or gases and are intended only for large dust particles.
C. Yes, if doubled up over the mouth.
D. Only in oxygen-deficient rooms.

TOS8_Section4.text: What safety rule applies when removing and disposing of contaminated disposable nitrile gloves after handling hazardous chemicals?
options: A. Wipe them clean with a paper towel and wear them home.
B. Remove them carefully using proper technique to avoid skin contact, discard them into hazardous solid waste, and wash hands immediately.
C. Wash them in the sink with dish soap and reuse them indefinitely.
D. Leave them on while touching door handles and phones.

TOS8_Section4.text: What safety precautions must be observed regarding long hair and loose jewelry in an organic laboratory?
options: A. Long hair must be securely tied back, and dangling jewelry or loose clothing removed to prevent entanglement in rotating or hot equipment.
B. Long hair acts as a natural fire blanket and needs no restraint.
C. Jewelry attracts static electricity to protect against sparks.
D. There are no restrictions on hair or jewelry.

TOS8_Section4.text: When is a Self-Contained Breathing Apparatus (SCBA) or supplied-air respirator strictly required instead of an air-purifying cartridge respirator?
options: A. During routine weighing of dry salt crystals on a balance
B. In oxygen-deficient atmospheres or Immediately Dangerous to Life or Health (IDLH) conditions
C. When working in an outdoor parking lot
D. Whenever wearing safety glasses

TOS8_Section4.text: What key concept describes the time it takes for a chemical hazardous substance to permeate completely through the material thickness of a protective glove?
options: A. Breakthrough time
B. Boiling point depression
C. Refractive index delay
D. Molecular weight velocity

TOS8_Section5.text: What do the signal words 'Danger' and 'Warning' indicate in the Globally Harmonized System (GHS) of classification and labeling?
options: A. 'Danger' is used for less severe hazards, while 'Warning' is used for severe hazards.
B. 'Danger' highlights more severe hazards, whereas 'Warning' designates less severe hazards.
C. Both words indicate identical hazard severity levels.
D. 'Danger' refers exclusively to physical fire risks, while 'Warning' refers to biological hazards.

TOS8_Section5.text: Which GHS hazard pictogram features a skull and crossbones inside a red-bordered square set at a point (diamond)?
options: A. Acute toxicity (fatal or toxic)
B. Environmental aquatic toxicity
C. Skin irritation and dermal sensitization
D. Compressed gas under pressure

TOS8_Section5.text: What type of chemical hazard does the GHS 'Health Hazard' pictogram (depicting a human torso with a starburst on the chest) represent?
options: A. Simple asphyxiants only
B. Carcinogenicity, respiratory sensitization, reproductive toxicity, mutagenicity, and target organ toxicity
C. Flammable solids and liquids
D. Corrosive metals

TOS8_Section5.text: Which GHS pictogram represents chemical oxidizers (substances that may cause or intensify fire)?
options: A. Exploding bomb
B. Flame over circle
C. Gas cylinder
D. Corrosion symbol

TOS8_Section5.text: What hazards are indicated by the GHS 'Corrosion' pictogram showing liquid pouring from two glass vials onto a metal plate and a human hand?
options: A. Flammable gas generation
B. Skin corrosion/burns, serious eye damage, and corrosivity to metals
C. Acute oral toxicity level 5
D. Simple cryogenic frostbite

TOS8_Section5.text: In GHS labeling codes, what do H-codes and P-codes stand for?
options: A. H-codes stand for Hazardous mass, P-codes stand for Pressure limits.
B. H-codes stand for Hazard statements, and P-codes stand for Precautionary statements.
C. H-codes stand for Heat capacity, and P-codes stand for Purity percentage.
D. H-codes stand for History logs, and P-codes stand for Protocol numbers.

TOS8_Section5.text: In the NFPA 704 'fire diamond' rating system, what hazard category is represented by the BLUE section on the left?
options: A. Flammability
B. Health hazard
C. Instability (reactivity)
D. Special physical hazards

TOS8_Section5.text: What does the RED section at the top of the NFPA 704 diamond indicate?
options: A. Flammability hazard
B. Radioactivity level
C. Biological infection risk
D. Corrosive acid strength

TOS8_Section5.text: What does a 'W' with a horizontal slash through it in the white (bottom) section of the NFPA 704 diamond signify?
options: A. Waste chemical container
B. Water-reactive substance (reacts violently or dangerously with water)
C. Weak electrical conductivity
D. Weight tolerance exceeded

TOS8_Section5.text: What is the numerical rating scale used in both NFPA 704 and HMIS hazard rating systems to indicate hazard severity?
options: A. 1 (severe) to 10 (low)
B. 0 (no hazard) to 4 (severe hazard)
C. A (lowest) to Z (highest)

TOS8_Section5.text: How does the Hazardous Materials Identification System (HMIS) differ visually from the NFPA 704 diamond?
options: A. HMIS uses colored horizontal bars with numerical ratings and a PPE code box, and includes a chronic health hazard asterisk in the blue bar.
B. HMIS uses a triangular yellow warning sign exclusively.
C. HMIS has no color coding.
D. HMIS is only used for shipping trucks.

TOS8_Section5.text: Under the UN / DOT transportation classification system for hazardous materials, what material category is designated as Class 3?
options: A. Explosives
B. Flammable liquids
C. Oxidizing agents
D. Radioactive materials

TOS8_Section5.text: Which DOT hazard class number is assigned to corrosive substances (acids and bases)?
options: A. Class 2
B. Class 5
C. Class 8
D. Class 9

TOS8_Section5.text: According to standard safety sign color conventions, what color is used to designate safe conditions, emergency exit routes, and first-aid equipment?
options: A. Bright red
B. Safety green
C. Vibrant yellow
D. Cobalt blue

TOS8_Section5.text: What safety meaning is communicated by a triangular yellow or amber safety sign with a black symbol?
options: A. Mandatory mandatory action
B. Warning or caution of potential physical/health hazards
C. Safe assembly point
D. Fire extinguisher location

TOS8_Section5.text: What shape and color combination represents a mandatory safety instruction sign (such as requiring safety glasses or gloves)?
options: A. Red circle with a slash through it
B. Blue circle with a white pictogram symbol
C. Green rectangle
D. Yellow triangle

TOS8_Section5.text: What labeling requirement applies to secondary workplace containers (such as wash bottles or temporary working beakers)?
options: A. They require no labels if used for less than 5 minutes.
B. They must be clearly labeled with the chemical identity and primary hazards.
C. They must feature barcoded pricing stickers.
D. They must display the manufacturer's home office address.

TOS8_Section5.text: What hazards are represented by the GHS 'Exclamation mark' pictogram?
options: A. Irritant, skin sensitizer, acute toxicity (harmful), narcotic effects, and respiratory tract irritation
B. Permanent total blindness and paralysis
C. Spontaneous combustion in air
D. Severe chronic organ failure

TOS8_Section5.text: What is the primary intended application of the NFPA 704 fire diamond rating system?
options: A. International ocean cargo shipping manifests
B. Stationary storage facilities, buildings, and emergency responders identifying facility hazards
C. Retail consumer food packaging labels
D. Personal clothing laundry instructions

TOS8_Section5.text: What was the purpose of replacing older European orange square hazard symbols (like T, Xi, F) with GHS red-bordered diamond pictograms?
options: A. To confuse students during examinations
B. To establish a unified, internationally harmonized standard for communicating chemical hazards globally
C. To reduce the cost of printing labels in black ink
D. To eliminate all warning symbols for non-hazardous reagents

TOS8_Section6.text: How many standardized sections comprise a modern Globally Harmonized System (GHS) compliant Safety Data Sheet (SDS)?
options: A. 8 sections
B. 12 sections
C. 16 sections
D. 20 sections

TOS8_Section6.text: What is the primary purpose of a Safety Data Sheet (SDS) in chemical management?
options: A. To provide retail marketing brochures and pricing lists
B. To provide comprehensive, detailed information regarding chemical hazards, safe handling, storage, emergency measures, and regulatory compliance
C. To serve as a legal receipt for tax deductions
D. To list the molecular weights of all known elements

TOS8_Section6.text: Which section of a standard GHS Safety Data Sheet covers First-Aid Measures?
options: A. Section 2
B. Section 4
C. Section 8
D. Section 13

TOS8_Section6.text: Where on an SDS would you look to find specific information regarding recommended Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) and occupational exposure limits (such as TLV or PEL)?
options: A. Section 1: Identification
B. Section 5: Fire-Fighting Measures
C. Section 8: Exposure Controls/Personal Protection
D. Section 12: Ecological Information

TOS8_Section6.text: Which SDS section details physical and chemical properties of the substance, including flash point, boiling point, vapor pressure, and appearance?
options: A. Section 3
B. Section 7
C. Section 9
D. Section 15

TOS8_Section6.text: Where should a laboratory worker look on an SDS to identify incompatible materials, conditions to avoid, and hazardous thermal decomposition products?
options: A. Section 2: Hazard Identification
B. Section 6: Accidental Release Measures
C. Section 10: Stability and Reactivity
D. Section 14: Transport Information

TOS8_Section6.text: Which SDS section contains toxicological data, including routes of exposure, acute toxicity estimates (such as $LD_{50}$), and carcinogenicity evaluations?
options: A. Section 11
B. Section 4
C. Section 9
D. Section 16

TOS8_Section6.text: What information is provided in Section 13 of an SDS?
options: A. Transport UN classification numbers
B. Disposal considerations and waste management guidance
C. Retail supplier telephone numbers
D. Detailed chemical synthesis pathways

TOS8_Section6.text: What does a CAS number uniquely identify when referenced on an SDS and chemical container label?
options: A. The highway shipping route code
B. A unique numerical identifier assigned by the Chemical Abstracts Service to every specific chemical substance
C. The manufacturing plant building number
D. The maximum legal storage temperature in Celsius

TOS8_Section6.text: Who is legally and primarily responsible for authoring and providing the Safety Data Sheet for a chemical product?
options: A. The chemical supplier, manufacturer, or importer
B. The municipal fire department
C. The individual undergraduate student worker
D. The local water district authority

TOS8_Section6.text: What is the fundamental operational difference between a chemical product container label and its complete Safety Data Sheet (SDS)?
options: A. The label provides a quick, concise summary of key hazards, while the SDS provides comprehensive, detailed technical documentation.
B. Labels are confidential and hidden, whereas SDS documents are public.
C. Labels contain 16 sections, while SDS documents contain only one.
D. There is no difference; they are identical documents.

TOS8_Section6.text: What critical item of documentation should always be brought along when seeking medical attention following a chemical exposure or injury?
options: A. The company's annual financial report
B. A copy of the chemical's Safety Data Sheet (SDS)
C. A blank laboratory notebook
D. The employee's driver's license

TOS8_Section6.text: Which SDS section outlines appropriate steps for spill cleanup, containment procedures, and emergency evacuation protocols?
options: A. Section 6: Accidental Release Measures
B. Section 2: Hazard Identification
C. Section 10: Stability and Reactivity
D. Section 15: Regulatory Information

TOS8_Section6.text: What does the abbreviation 'SDS' stand for, replacing what older terminology?
options: A. Standardized Data System, replacing Material Data Sheets
B. Safety Data Sheet, replacing Material Safety Data Sheet (MSDS)
C. Solute Density Specification, replacing Mass Solution Data
D. Systematic Diagnostic Sheet, replacing Medical Safety Diagnosis

TOS8_Section6.text: Where on an SDS would you find transport-specific regulatory details such as the UN shipping identification number and packing group?
options: A. Section 3
B. Section 11
C. Section 14
D. Section 16

TOS8_Section6.text: What is the purpose of Section 1 (Identification) on an SDS?
options: A. To list acute oral rat $LD_{50}$ values
B. To provide the product identifier, manufacturer name, address, recommended use, and emergency telephone contact
C. To detail fire extinguisher types
D. To provide ecological half-life data in soil

TOS8_Section6.text: Under worker 'Right-to-Know' and hazard communication standards, who must have ready and immediate access to Safety Data Sheets in the workplace?
options: A. Only corporate board executives
B. All workers who handle or may be exposed to hazardous chemical substances
C. General public visitors touring the building lobby
D. Only certified safety inspectors

TOS8_Section6.text: Which SDS section details appropriate fire-fighting measures, including suitable extinguishing media and hazardous combustion byproducts?
options: A. Section 5
B. Section 2
C. Section 12
D. Section 7

TOS8_Section6.text: Why is it important to verify the revision date listed on an SDS before relying on its data?
options: A. Outdated sheets may contain old hazard classifications or obsolete exposure limits as toxicological knowledge evolves.
B. SDS documents expire legally after exactly 24 hours.
C. Revision dates determine the market price of the chemical.
D. Older sheets transform into colored paper.

TOS8_Section6.text: What information is summarized in Section 2 of an GHS-compliant SDS?
options: A. Chemical composition formulas
B. Hazard identification, classification, signal words, pictograms, hazard statements (H-codes), and precautionary statements (P-codes)
C. Physical melting and boiling temperatures
D. Supplier corporate history

TOS10_Section1B.text: What is the primary characteristic of a representative sample?
options: A. It is taken exclusively from the top layer of a bulk shipment
B. Its composition accurately reflects the composition of the entire lot
C. It consists of a single increment collected at a random time
D. It has been completely dissolved and diluted prior to measurement

TOS10_Section1B.text: Which term refers to the actual small portion of material that is directly measured or analyzed in the laboratory?
options: A. Gross sample
B. Increment
C. Test sample
D. Lot

TOS10_Section1B.text: How do sampling variance and analytical variance interact to determine total variance?
options: A. total variance = sampling variance * analytical variance
B. total variance = sampling variance + analytical variance
C. total variance = sampling variance - analytical variance
D. total variance = sampling variance / analytical variance

TOS10_Section1B.text: Why is taking a single scoop from the top of a bag or pile of solid material considered unrepresentative?
options: A. Volatile components always evaporate from the surface
B. Particles segregate by size and density during handling
C. Top layers absorb atmospheric nitrogen rapidly
D. Surface particles naturally undergo oxidation

TOS10_Section1B.text: Which sampling strategy divides a population with distinct zones or layers into sub-groups before sampling each group?
options: A. Systematic sampling
B. Simple random sampling
C. Stratified sampling
D. Judgmental sampling

TOS10_Section1B.text: What type of sample is collected at a single specific time and location to measure instantaneous conditions?
options: A. Composite sample
B. Grab sample
C. Aliquot sample
D. Integrated sample

TOS10_Section1B.text: What sampling device is used to collect solid increments across different depths of a stationary powder or grain pile?
options: A. Cross-cut sampler
B. Sampling thief (spear or probe)
C. Gas-sampling bulb
D. Niskin bottle

TOS10_Section1B.text: Which solid sample reduction technique uses a chute with alternating opposite-facing slots to yield two equal halves?
options: A. Coning and quartering
B. Rotary sample divider
C. Riffle splitter
D. Mortar and pestle

TOS10_Section1B.text: When preparing a solid sample for trace metal analysis, which grinding material should be avoided to prevent iron, chromium, and nickel contamination?
options: A. Agate
B. Stainless steel
C. Ceramic
D. Tungsten carbide

TOS10_Section1B.text: When sampling water for volatile organic compounds (VOCs) or dissolved gases, how should the sample bottle be filled?
options: A. Filled to 50% capacity to allow oxygen exposure
B. Filled completely with zero headspace or air bubbles
C. Left with a 10% volume headspace for expansion
D. Kept unstoppered until arrival at the laboratory

TOS10_Section1B.text: What action should be performed before collecting a tap water sample for chemical analysis?
options: A. Rinse the container with nitric acid
B. Flush the line to clear stagnant water
C. Boil the water to eliminate dissolved gases
D. Filter the water through a 0.2 micrometer membrane on-site

TOS10_Section1B.text: Which parameter must be measured on-site immediately after collection due to rapid changes?
options: A. Total mercury
B. Dissolved oxygen
C. Organochlorine pesticides
D. Heavy metal content

TOS10_Section1B.text: What is the standard preservation method for preserving metal analytes in water samples to prevent precipitation and adsorption to container walls?
options: A. Addition of NaOH to pH greater than 12
B. Addition of HNO3 to pH less than 2
C. Addition of Na2S2O3
D. Storage at room temperature in open clear glass

TOS10_Section1B.text: Why are glass containers preferred over plastic containers for collecting samples intended for organic compound analysis?
options: A. Plastic can shatter under refrigeration
B. Plastic can leach phthalates or adsorb organic species
C. Glass shields the sample from ambient magnetic fields
D. Glass reacts with organic solvents to stabilize them

TOS10_Section1B.text: What is the main purpose of adding sodium thiosulfate to a water sample prior to analysis?
options: A. Lower the pH below 2.0
B. Neutralize residual chlorine
C. Digest suspended insoluble organic particles
D. Prevent metal ion oxidation

TOS10_Section1B.text: What term describes the maximum permissible elapsed time between sample collection and laboratory analysis?
options: A. Retention period
B. Chain of custody
C. Holding time
D. Shelf life

TOS10_Section1B.text: Which quality control sample travels sealed from the laboratory to the field site and back to detect contamination during transport and storage?
options: A. Field duplicate
B. Equipment blank
C. Trip blank
D. Method blank

TOS10_Section1B.text: What quality control tool documents every individual who handled a sample, along with transfer dates and times, to maintain legal and technical traceability?
options: A. Sampling plan
B. Safety Data Sheet
C. Chain of custody
D. Standard operating procedure

TOS10_Section1B.text: Which quality control sample involves passing clean water through cleaned sampling apparatus in the field to confirm effective decontamination?
options: A. Equipment (rinsate) blank
B. Trip blank
C. Field blank
D. Blind spike

TOS10_Section1B.text: When collecting a water sample from a flowing stream or river, how should the container be oriented relative to the current?
options: A. Opening facing downstream, away from the current
B. Opening facing upstream, into the current
C. Opening facing toward the river bank
D. Container held horizontally at the water surface film
